thread:
evan: FYI — Lantern asked for a migration playbook from CompetitorX -> Redwood. Top asks: prompt parity, response diffs, pricing delta, and security questionnaire. Can we sketch a POC timeline?
shreya: propose a compatibility shim + canonical prompt set. start with ~50 prompt pairs (happy/path/edge) and run semantic parity evals. keep it lightweight.
kyle: pricing quick note — CompetitorX bills per-request + slot. For Redwood, show hosted per-token + reserved capacity options. rough estimate: same throughput, ~0.8x token cost with quantized variant; reserved pool pricing will be a separate line.
maria: security Qs they listed: SOC2, KMS integration, VPC peering, audit logs, data residency controls. do we have canned answers for their vendor questionnaire?
legalbot: uploaded standard answer pack v2.1 for SOC2/KMS. flag: Lantern asked for explicit contract language on model-output IP and indemnity — legal review required.
infra-oncall: for the POC we'll provision a dedicated pool in us-west1. need their egress IPs for whitelisting and a CIDR for VPC peering. stand-up ETA ~3 business days once we have IPs/creds.
shreya: prompt parity tactics: normalization layer to map CompetitorX params (temperature/top_p) + align tokenization. add a post-processing hook to normalize punctuation/whitespace differences. include deterministic seeding for parity tests.
evan: can someone drop a quick curl mapping example we can hand to their engs to reduce integration friction?
kyle: I can do a quick mapping example.
shreya: ```
# example mapping CompetitorX -> Redwood (conceptual)
POST /v1/redwood/generate 
{
  "model": "rwd-1-std",
  "prompt": "{{user_prompt}}",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "max_tokens": 512
}
# Notes: map CompetitorX temp->temperature, remap stop tokens, run tokenizer diff to normalize token counts
```
maria: for the security packet I'll attach: SOC2 summary (redacted), KMS integration spec, network topology diagram, and our data handling addendum. I'll have a draft by EOD tomorrow.
evan: proposed timeline: Day 0-3 infra + network (whitelist + pool); Day 4-7 import prompt set & parity evals; Day 8-10 perf + cost benchmarks; Day 11 results + pricing & contract draft. realistic?
infra-oncall: yes, assuming they provide IPs and test creds quickly.
legalbot: we'll need the reserved-capacity SKU and SOW language to draft the contract. also add the data handling addendum to SOW.
shreya: expect some small response deltas (entity formatting, punctuation). include an acceptance QA checklist: WER threshold, hallucination cap, token delta limit. plan for one manual review pass for ambiguous cases.
evan: owners: infra-oncall (infra), shreya (evals & shim), kyle (pricing), maria (security packet), legalbot (contract). I'll run a weekly sync. :thumbsup:
kyle: pricing deliverable: show example numbers for 10M tokens/month with hosted per-token and reserved-monthly commit so they can compare line-item impact.
maria: shared draft security packet here: https://redwood.internal/docs/poc-security/lantern-packet (internal link).
evan: thanks — I'll forward this plan to Lantern and set kickoff for Wed 9am PT.
shreya: one more item — add a smoke-test harness that replays 100 queries from the prompt set and diffs token counts + semantic similarity to catch regressions early.
evan: perfect. I'll create action cards in presales board and mark owners. :rocket:
